To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2x2 block preconditioner is more effective than the Krylov method and fixed-point iteration for solving nonsymmetric linear equations.

the preconditioners proposed in this paper have the potential to be competitive with other state-of-the-art methods, especially in the context of Krylov subspace methods, but they are not yet competitive in practice.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of iterative methods for the solution of large-scale systems of linear equations.
the design and implementation of robust and efficient preconditioners for the iterative solution of large-scale systems of linear equations.
the design and analysis of efficient iterative methods for solving large sparse linear algebra problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the 2x2-block preconditioners is not always beneficial for the solution of the nonsymmetric problems, and it may be harmful.
, the 2x2 block preconditioning method is the most efficient and effective method to solve the linear system of equation in the present study.
there are no general rules to be followed for the selection of a preconditioner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, we have shown that the block Krylov method can be used to solve the saddle point problem.
we have developed a novel preconditioning technique that can solve the large-scale linear systems arising from the discretization of PDEs with high-order finite elements.
the use of a $2\timestwo$ block preconditioner can lead to a significant reduction in the number of iterations and/or the computational work per iteration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the preconditioner should be chosen based on the eigenvalues of the original system.
the preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) method is not a good choice for nonsymmetric problems, and that a better choice is the preconditioned minimal residual (P-MINRES) method.
the preconditioners we have developed are robust and can be applied to a wide variety of problems.
